correctness.rationale: Factor A as a nonzero column times a nonzero row; independent base changes reduce it to E11 while preserving the predicates and transporting fibers bijectively. In this basis the product difference is UJV with shared first-row/first-column data t and independent lower blocks supplying q^{2h} lifts. The top-left coefficient vanishes and rank is at most two, including characteristic two. In rank two both factors have full rank. Both zero axes force t=0 and the usual GL2 number of factorizations; exactly one zero axis is impossible; both nonzero axes with zero corner impose one nonzero determinant value, giving an SL2 coset. For the terse rank-one step at line 64: if t is nonzero and the first row vanishes, every column of V is in ker(tJ)=span(t^T). A vanishing first column then forces UJt^T=0, hence the entire target is zero. Thus rank one with both axes zero really does force t=0. Count lower-block factorizations by the dimension of the first factor's image (one or two) to get the claimed fiber. With one zero axis and one nonzero axis, t is nonzero, one factor is forced by that axis and the other has one linear condition per lower row (or column). A rank-one target with both axes nonzero cannot have corner zero. The zero count splits into t=0 (unconstrained lower-block zero-product pairs) and t nonzero (q^{alpha+beta} solutions per such t, given the two vanishing axes). The sum gives exactly equation (26). All target counts follow by the rank-one scalar quotient, the standard rank-two block count, and (for both axes nonzero) q^{alpha+beta-1} lower blocks per nonzero axis pair. To see the last count directly, for Z=(0,r;c,D) with c,r nonzero, rank two means D=c s+t r; the map (s,t) to D has a one-dimensional kernel. Independent enumeration matched every target in (2,2,2), (2,3,3) and (3,3,3) and the target-class counts; at (3,3,3) sorted in the table's order the counts are 32,72,72,48,1728, with reduced rank-two fiber sizes 48 and 24. The zero fibers were 88,29889,6987465 respectively.
